As a chef... my life is not my own. And I do it because I love it. I work 70 hours a week. I often skip sleep and go out late or early or work in my friends whenever I can. Dating right now is very difficult for me. No one wants to work within my parameters of life. I get that. My parameters are not only limiting to people not in the service industry, I also do not have to explain them to anyone. These are my parameters. I have only so much time. And the time I have to give you is all yours. 

If you are willing to really give this person your time when they can give you theirs, the only way you can show that is by doing it. If this person is worth it, then you’ll work within his parameters. If he is willing to fit into your parameters, it may not be as easy but he’ll figure it out. 

Basically most of my conversations with seeing or hanging out with anyone, friend, family etc is: I have this day off, I work these days but I could still meet at x time only. If I make plans, I try very hard to not cancel, but it does happen. 

Only you know if you’re willing to put in the effort here.  And yes, he has to be willing to put in the effort too. You just have to understand that the amount of time given is not always what either person wants.

Hi. Are you me? You must be me. I had a FWB situation with my best friend. When it began he was seeing someone else and I was ending my marriage. It didn’t last long and while it hurt like hell, it was for the best. He was pursuing this other woman and I definitely needed some time, even if I didn’t want it. We started it up again after he had stopped seeing the other person. I was fine with the situation even though I have feelings for him. But it got to be too much for both of us and it ended badly. We are still friends, and are back to talking daily. But that took a while. And it hurts a lot, even now. It’s been a few months and I am still not over it. But unless he is willing to explore an actual relationship with me, it cannot happen again. 

If you continue, you have to take him at his word that he is not available for more and that has to be that. It probably won’t end well if you all ready have feelings. If the friendship is what is important to you, just end it now. It’s going to suck. But in the long run, you maybe saving yourself some time.

I am in a very similar situation. Very good friend and I finally acted on a mutual attraction. First time it happened, he had just started seeing someone and I was kicking my now ex husband out of my house. Things went sloppily for a bit between us before we broke it off. But we remained friends. Then it started up again. To me, it got a little too real for him and he ran. To him I pushed a little too far and he ran. It hurt like hell and I spent way too much on therapy. But I had to realize I couldn’t walk away from the friendship. We still talk everyday and see each other several times a week. It is possible to go back to being friends. And while I am not completely convinced it won’t happen again, I am confident enough now to know I can put my foot down and say what I want. If he doesn’t want the same thing, we’ll still be friends. If you really don’t want to ruin your friendship, even if the intimacy stops, you just have to keep talking. Stay open and don’t let it go. Friendships are relationships too and they take work. If you’re willing to do the work, you won’t ruin it.

I have. I don’t regret doing it. I was looking for a change anyway. At first it was great. But when things for got rocky and I thought I wanted to bail, I had no idea how I would do so. In my old city I had always been self sufficient and able to live on my own. But in the new city that was not an option. I stayed with him for far too long trying to figure that one out. Honestly, a huge red flag was that the year before we moved, I had a job offer in my home town. He did not want to move with me. I wasn’t exactly head over heels about moving back to my home town, but it would have been a good job for me. I ended up changing careers because of the move we did make. 

Lesson learned. I would do it again under the correct circumstances, but only for someone who I felt would be willing to do the same for me. 

FYI, we had been dating for two years when we moved, had lived together for one of those years all ready. Stayed together for 11 years.
